translation_notes: The FILTER calls a custom SPARQL extension function, tfun:isDuring(?a, ?b), registered on rdflib's global operator table by importing the `timefuncs` package (register_custom_function in timefuncs/__init__.py). That registration is orthogonal to the island construction: s{ } embeds the query text verbatim and rdflib validates it as plain SPARQL syntax at transpile time -- a FunctionCall to an unregistered IRI is syntactically valid and only fails at evaluation time if the function is not registered when the query actually runs. `timefuncs` IS on PyPI (`pip index versions timefuncs` -> 0.1.4, requiring only rdflib>=6.0.0, satisfied by the pinned 7.2.1) but is not installed in this shared venv, and this session does not install packages into it while other agents translate other strata concurrently -- same shim approach as the sibling test_is_after region (whose note says merely 'not installable', which this note corrects), so `_context.py` reproduces the registration side effect, copying `is_during`, the private helper `is_contained_by` it delegates to, and `is_contained_by`'s own helper `_path_exists` verbatim from RDFLib/timefuncs@dd3bde8727 (real logic needed: the region's `expected` list only matches the real predicate semantics against the real data).

Context restored (see original.py/translated.ldpy headers): `from pathlib import Path`, elided by line-range extraction (used one context line down by `tests_dir = Path(__file__).parent`, which WAS captured). The real input graph, `tests/functions/data/is_during.ttl`, is restored verbatim at data/is_during.ttl since `test_is_during` builds its own graph from that fixed relative path rather than taking one as an argument -- so there is no fixture.ttl for this region (see driver.py); the real file covers 9 a/b pairs, all designed to be tfun:isDuring matches by construction (declared intervalDuring/intervalContains, transitive chains of both, hasBeginning/hasEnd interval comparisons, and inXSDDateTimeStamp-based calculation) -- the assert's `expected` list is exactly these 9 pairs, so any spurious extra match (e.g. a cross pair like a01/b02) or missing one fails the comparison; this is the actual regression fixture the real project checks tfun:isDuring against.

The query itself is a plain two-variable SELECT with one FILTER calling the custom function -- no UNION/OPTIONAL/paths/aggregates, but FILTER alone already puts it outside m{ }'s coverage (querying.md: 'No FILTER, OPTIONAL, UNION, property paths or aggregates'), so s{ } is the correct, not just the sampled, construction here.

initNs={"time": TIME, "tfun": TFUN} disappears entirely: the prologue is built from @prefix time:/tfun: declared at file scope (querying.md 'The prologue is the block's'), a single vocabulary declaration instead of a dict rebuilt at every call site -- and ID, used only in Python code (never in the query text), becomes an ordinary @prefix too, so `str(ID.a01)` reads `str(id:a01)`.

The original test only asserts and returns nothing (same situation as lazlop/semantic_objects's test_class_scope_or_roundtrip and the sibling test_is_after in this stratum): `return actual` was appended identically to both original.py and translated.ldpy purely so run_pair has a value to diff; it changes nothing about the RDF behaviour under test.
